newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Jan 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Jan 24.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Ayalas and Lopezes, the country's two richest and most prominent business clans, won the concessions to operate and manage the countrys' biggest waterworks and sewerage system. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER, PHILIPPINE STAR)
- Colleagues of detained congressman Romeo Jalosjos vote against his suspension. (MANILA TIMES AND TODAY)
- Presidential aspirant Senator Gloria Macapagal Arroyo quits the main opposition party Laban ng Demokratikong Pilipino (MANILA BULLETIN)
- The government declares a ceasefire with the Moro Islamic Liberation Front following clashes earlier this week which left 41 people dead, officials say (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
- The National Economic and Development Authority says the 20 peso wage increase is beyond what the economy can absorb. (BUSINESSWORLD)
- Industrialist Raul Concepcion warns early deregulation of the oil industry can cause spiralling inflation which will be detrimental to the country's global competitiveness. (BUSINESS DAILY)
- The Department of Finance will issue an order that will remove the foreign exchange forward cover on oil imports. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
- The Securities and Exchange Commission freezes the share prices of Itogon Suyoc Mines A and B at the Philippine Stock Exchange. (MANILA TIMES)
